reason: MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 2.1 re-read verbatim: STRAITREP area 100 40'E to 104 23'E 'includes the routeing system in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore'; para 3.4 assigns Sectors 1-5 to Klang VTS. MPA Operational Areas page (last updated 28 Sep 2026) repeats Sectors 1-5 = Klang VTS, giving current evidence that Klang VTS is the operating authority. SPI 2026 (updated 17 Apr 2026) Annex 2 coordinates (101 12.32'E to 101 38.71'E) and Appendix 1 chartlet (p.119) place the scheme in Sector 2 Jugra with the SE end at the Sector 2/3 line off Port Dickson; both Klang VTS. Sector 1-6 limits are graphical only, as the record already states.

SPI 2026 Annex 3 coordinates (101 36.01'E to 102 00.91'E) and Appendix 1 chartlet show the scheme between the Sector 2/3 line off Port Dickson and the Sector 3/4 line off Malacca, i.e. Sector 3 Cape Rachado with the SE end near Sector 4; all Klang VTS per MSC.73(69) para 3.4 and the current MPA table (28 Sep 2026). Wholly within the STRAITREP area.

Classification VTS + MRS (Klang VTS Sectors 4-5, Johor VTS Sector 6, marginal Singapore VTS Sector 7) is upheld. Correct one detail in vts_boundary_basis: my side-of-line recalculation against the Tg Piai (01 15.50N 103 30.75E) to Pulau Karimun Kecil (01 09.20N 103 24.35E) reporting line (MSC.73(69) Annex 1 para 3.3.1; MPA page defines Sector 7 from this line to 103 44.5'E) puts point (70) about 0.05 nm east of the line, but (58) about 0.7 nm, (59) about 1.2 nm and (76) about 1.6 nm east. The Sector 7 portion is therefore up to about 1.6 nm, not 'well under 1 nm'. The SPI Appendix 2 chartlet (p.120) confirms the lane ends and the separation zone tip lie just east of the Piai to Karimun line before the Off Sultan Shoal precautionary area. Points (57), (60), (69), (75) are west of the line.

MPA 'Vessels arriving in Singapore' page (last updated 28 Sep 2026) defines Sector 7 as between the Tg Piai to Pulau Karimun Kecil line and Long 103 44.5'E, and Sector 8 as 103 44.5'E to 104 02.1'E, both Singapore VTS (VTIS West Ch 73, VTIS Central Ch 14). SPI Annex 5 coordinates (103 32.20'E to 103 49.55'E) put the western end points 5.8 to 7.8 nm east of the Piai line by my calculation, so the scheme lies in Sectors 7 and 8 as recorded. Minor note: the same MPA page gives 103 44.6'E in one paragraph and 103 44.5'E in the sector table; this does not affect the VTS attribution.

SPI Annex 6 coordinates (103 50.21'E to 103 52.66'E) lie wholly between 103 44.5'E and 104 02.1'E, which is Sector 8, VTIS Central, Singapore VTS (MPA page updated 28 Sep 2026; SPI Appendix 2 chartlet).

SPI Annex 7 coordinates run from 103 53.75'E to 104 03.48'E, crossing the Sector 8/9 limit at 104 02.1'E (MPA page; Appendix 2 chartlet). Both are Singapore VTS sectors. Well within the STRAITREP area.

Partial coverage confirmed. SPI Annex 8 gives the scheme as 104 14.89'E to 104 27.84'E. MSC.73(69) para 2.1 ends STRAITREP at 104 23'E. The MPA page defines Sector 9 as 104 02.1'E to 104 23.0'E. The SPI Appendix 2 chartlet draws the Sector 9 limit as a thin dashed meridian at 'Long 104 22.9'E', with the TSS outline continuing north-east past it and past Horsburgh Light. The purple dashed lines beyond the meridian are the TSS limits, not a sector boundary. Caveat to add: the MPA page tells ships approaching from the east to report to VTIS East when Horsburgh Lt (104 24.337'E) is abeam, so the VTS engages ships in the eastern part of the scheme. Under the rule against treating a VHF reporting point as VTS coverage, this does not extend the defined sector, so 'partial' remains correct. About 35 to 40 per cent of the scheme's longitudinal extent is outside the defined area.

Downgrade from VTS + MRS to VTS only, with a currency caveat. (1) Quote verified on the live Hubla page (22 Jun 2020): VTS Merak and VTS Benoa are 'siap untuk melaksanakan pengawasan di seluruh wilayah TSS di Selat Sunda dan Selat Lombok', and ships in the Sunda Strait TSS use VHF 22 or 68, call sign Merak VTS. (2) Currency: I found no official post-2020 statement that Merak VTS operates over the TSS. The only later item is a 2024 peer-reviewed paper (IJOCE vol 8 no 2) on 'The Role of Merak VTS in the Implementation of TSS in Sunda Strait', which is non-official and supports continued operation only indirectly. The 2020 release is still published on the official portal and has not been superseded, and the TSS is in force. I judge the VTS link acceptable if it is flagged as resting on 2020 official evidence plus 2024 secondary evidence. A strict reading of the currency rule ('only historical evidence' leads to Unresolved) would instead make this Unresolved. The coordinator should decide and record which. (3) SUNDAREP should not be counted as an MRS. The source says it is 'wajib' only for 'semua kapal berbendera Indonesia'. Foreign ships, which make up the international transit traffic the TSS serves, are only 'sangat dianjurkan' (strongly recommended) to take part. It is not an IMO-adopted SRS (absent from the Part I baseline), and the KM 129/130 texts have not been read. Record SUNDAREP under voluntary_reporting for foreign ships, with a note that it is mandatory for Indonesian-flag ships under national decree. Set mandatory_reporting to 'No (national flag-state scheme only)'.

Downgrade from VTS + MRS to VTS only, with a currency caveat. (1) The Hubla 22 Jun 2020 release is verified: VTS Benoa is ready to monitor the whole Lombok Strait TSS, VHF 16 or 68, call sign Benoa VTS. (2) Post-2020 evidence: IDX Channel (14 Nov 2022) quotes DG Sea Transportation Arif Toha: 'Kita siagakan 2 kapal navigasi, VTS dan SROP di Pelabuhan Benoa untuk monitoring keselamatan pelayaran di Perairan Alur Benoa dan TSS Selat Lombok.' This is a media report of an official statement (Tier 3). The Hubla microsite copy could not be retrieved because the portal has migrated. No official 2023 to 2026 confirmation was found. As with TSS-0153, the VTS link is acceptable only if flagged. A strict reading of the currency rule makes it Unresolved. (3) LOMBOKREP is mandatory only for Indonesian-flag ships and strongly recommended for foreign ships. It is not IMO-adopted. Record it as voluntary for foreign ships, with a national flag-state mandatory note, not as an MRS.

Marine Department fact sheet verified: the VTS 'covers all navigable waters of Hong Kong used by sea-going vessels and ferries', and TSS 'are implemented in the East Lamma Channel and Tathong Channel'. The Guide to Hong Kong waters (March 2026 Edition, p.8) lists the Tathong Channel TSS within Hong Kong waters. The VTC pamphlet (April 2025) lists 'Tathong Channel Separation Buoy No. 1' as an Eastern Approaches (Channel 12) calling-in point. The sector chart 2025MAR032 is dated September 2025. No IMO Part I or other separate mandatory reporting scheme applies. Mandatory VTS participation under Cap 313A is correctly recorded as VTS participation, so VTS only is correct. One weakness: the September 2025 chart has no extractable text naming the Tathong buoy, so that calling-in point rests on the pamphlet.
